page: Microsoft Azure M16s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv3 family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile is driven by an x86_64 Intel processor featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of system memory. This yields a 16:1 memory-to-core ratio, delivering 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without any discrete graphics acceleration hardware.

Storage configuration on the M16s_v3 provides no integrated local disk space, meaning ephemeral or persistent data must be managed through attached remote storage volumes. The virtual machine supports Azure Premium Storage to deliver predictable input and output performance over virtualized channels. Networking assigns zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, requiring allocation through virtual network gateways or associated Azure public IP resources.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high RAM density makes the M16s_v3 qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound software stacks. Deployments that require vast working memory sets can run without the expense of over-provisioning unneeded CPU cores. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, which introduces a dependency on networked disk throughput and latency for persistence.

The M16s_v3 is suited for memory-intensive production workloads, including enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, data warehousing staging buffers, and relational database management systems requiring extensive caching layers.

The M16s_v3 is primarily designed for high-capacity in-memory databases, memory-backed distributed caching systems, relational database management systems, and large-scale enterprise applications requiring broad working memory buffers.
